purpose: Literature-informed engineering scenarios, not patient data or a diagnostic simulator

sources.finding: Repeated fridge checking is explicitly described; memory, reassurance and context matter.
sources.limit: No appliance-specific frequency, interval or diagnostic cutoff is supplied.

sources.finding: Six people with dementia, 22 kitchen-task recordings: sequencing including repetition and omission, finding objects, appliance operation and incoherence.
sources.limit: Mapping these task errors to microwave restarts is an engineering hypothesis, not a measured restart distribution.

sources.finding: Longitudinal home tea-making observations found individual differences and omissions as the most common error class.
sources.limit: Omission is not repetition; retained routines must not automatically be labelled abnormal.

sources.finding: Caregiver-labelled normal, repetitive and sleep-disturbance sensor records from one dementia patient.
sources.limit: No raw data imported. Single environment, motion sensors, not universal HA state thresholds; printed collection dates are inconsistent.

sources.finding: Longitudinal monitoring reports cooking decline, a stove left on and a reported microwave setting error.
sources.limit: Safety and omission observations do not establish repetition thresholds; the microwave explanation is participant reported.

sources.finding: Models task execution with memory and sequencing/completion errors.
sources.limit: Conceptual model, real-user validation still required. This project does not implement ACT-R or infer dementia severity.

sources.finding: Introduces synthetic abnormal activities into smart-home datasets and evaluates anomaly detection.
sources.limit: Synthetic labels do not constitute clinically observed dementia episodes. We reuse the evaluation idea, not its CNN.

sources.finding: Synthetic and real activity durations differ for several tasks, motivating calibration.
sources.limit: Reported regression performance is not evidence of Pauseable clinical accuracy; no regression coefficients copied.

sources.finding: Kitchen activity and transition patterns across 73 dementia/MCI households, with a 21-household pandemic subset.
sources.limit: Mixed occupancy and no repetitive-event labels. Released fridge events are not open/close pairs; oven-use is not a guaranteed microwave; timezone unspecified.

sources.finding: 36 participants (12 HC, 13 SCD, 11 MCI) used kettle, toaster and hot plate tasks. Features included counts, duration and inaction; sensor/power outages caused missing tasks.
sources.limit: No diagnosed dementia cohort, no washer data, no clinical repetition cutoff. Raw data require author request. Only design rationale is used; no patient rows or fitted coefficients imported.

sources.finding: 130 participants, including 13 with dementia, completed eight tasks. Preparatory, action and concluding omissions were separately coded; microwave water heating was an action step.
sources.limit: Observed omissions are distinct from repetition and cannot be recovered from appliance counts alone. No raw participant data imported.

sources.finding: Kitchen task dataset contains scripted normal and erroneous behavior performed by actors.
sources.limit: Actors are not a dementia patient cohort. Used to justify explicit simulated provenance, not to train a clinical model or claim patient accuracy.

parameters.basis: Engineering sensitivity grid only. Intensity describes injected event density, NOT dementia severity. No numeric values estimated from a clinical paper.

scenarios.interpretation: Possible checking loop; intent unobservable in door events.
Cold meal preparation; deliberately identical to fridge_recheck sensor events.
Hypothetical task restart mapped to microwave operation; not a measured clinical distribution.
Separate portions; deliberately identical to microwave_restart events.
Engineering reference: a two-second door opening followed by one heating cycle.
One night use is not a diagnosis or necessarily unwanted behavior.
Multiple household users can produce a busy appliance stream; identity is not observed.
Fridge access without cooking could also mean a cold meal. Not a repetitive positive label.
A long heating operation tests a coverage gap in count features; not a clinical duration cutoff.
Exact duplicate deliveries must not create extra physical actions.
Missing closure/coverage must not be called a confirmed omission or normal period.
Engineering variation spreading checks across two hours; gap is not a patient statistic.
Slower task execution with few interactions must not be labelled repetitive merely for taking longer; no published duration copied.
Engineering analogy of task rechecking applied to washer power; no washer-specific dementia evidence. Running/idle encode the existing demo's power adapter, not physical washing.
Power adjustment during setup has observations identical to washer_power_recheck. No clinical positive label.
One simulated physical operation with automatic completion must not become multiple manual restarts.
